reviews.text: The build-up to this climax is slow but is masterfully done without being too sentimental, and Granik seems to understand how to deliver an emotional moment without being manipulative.
reviews.author: Bianca Garner

reviews.text: Foster and McKenzie not only give great individual performances, but their chemistry together is stunning and it made for an emotional experience that few movies matched in 2018.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: The beauty of it all is while the characters find any means necessary to erase their existence from the world, they will surely find a way to creep into and leave a trace in your heart.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: Both performances are superbly acted by Foster and McKenzie, with McKenzie being the shining star. This is expected in Granik’s films now...
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: The writing and direction by Debra Granik is sharp and sure. This has the lean, spare look of a low-budget independent film, but it is emotionally rich and powerful.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: “Leave No Trace” struck a chord with me early, and I could feel its emotional tug all the way till the end. It’s not a movie deeply concerned with plot. Instead it is all about character.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Ben Foster gives the performance of his career – it’s a knockout. Leave No Trace doesn’t have a false note in it.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Granik brilliantly delivers the viewer into the characters' spatially and socially secluded world, making otherwise normal, crowded living environments seem oppressive and even dangerous by comparison.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: a truly superb drama that offers no answers and just takes viewers along for the ride.
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: Writer-director Debra Granik's take on PTSD in military veterans is of course compassionate but perhaps slightly less tolerant of the isolation that her male protagonist...
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Debra Granik's Leave No Trace is a gripping drama...
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: Despite the heartbreaking stories she tells, she gives them (particularly the young women in her films) a flicker of hope in the darkness.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: [It] concerns itself with individuals attempting to exist outside societal norms and, in doing so, proves to be a moving study of love, loss and what it means to truly belong.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: Debra Granik's Leave No Trace is a gem of a film.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Where their story goes from here isn't always easy to watch, but thanks to McKenzie and Foster's fully committed performances and Granik's nuanced direction, it's powerful and compelling.
reviews.author: Betsy Bozdech

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a slow burn, and carefully constructed; the performances are measured and calm. There's no need to overplay the drama - the circumstances presented here are serious enough as they are.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: ...Foster's most subtle performance and an exciting debut from both Debra and McKenzie who I can't wait to see more out of.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: I loved Director Debra Granick's feature Leave No Trace, which captures a pulled-from-life sense of surviving off the grid in Pacific Northwest forests.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: While the film alludes to larger societal problems such as America's treatment of veterans, and inflexible, societal views about what it means to be a caregiver, the primary narrative focus is on an intimate relationship between two people...
reviews.author: Jim Rohner

reviews.text: This is director Debra Granik's first fiction feature since ... Winter's Bone, and it's been worth the wait.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is wonder to behold, a hard watch made even harder by the fact that it really happened. It is a truly American story of love, survival and acceptance in our country's often forgotten frontier.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Leave No Trace should start a healthy conversation while providing a heartfelt story that doesn't ring false even once during its 110 minutes.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: One of the very best films of the year.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Taps into the gut-wrenching possibilities of the kindness of humanity; it is delicately compelling and intricately detailed.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: Another tour de force from Granik - a filmmaker who instinctively knows how to alchemise the dramatic, cinematographic and anthropological elements of her stories so acutely.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: It is not an easy thing to place us into the lives of people we've never had real-life contact with, but this is the stuff that fuels Granik's creativity, and Leave No Trace is a fresh reminder of her talent.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: [Granik] strikes a keen balance of examining the characters like an anthropologist would study another culture, but she never becomes too detached.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a brilliant examination of family, sacrifice and the price a parent is willing to pay so his child can lead a better life.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a deeply affecting but ultimately universal tale of children leaving home to embark on an independent life. Letting go may be painful, but it's a necessary process.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Delivers something so full of strength and sadness that anyone who calls it slow should have to take a 100-level course in humanity.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Granik has drawn yet another deeply affecting portrait of families who live on the margins - sometimes by choice, often because of circumstance. Her images of poverty are warmly generous, yet free of condescension or romanticisation.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Script, direction, and acting all work together to deliver a story that clearly communicates what is at stake for its characters and what they represent with a rare subtle intelligence.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Leave No Trace will undoubtedly leave many impressions, as it is a beautiful and expertly made film that shouldn't be overlooked.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: What I most appreciate about Granik's approach is how she eschews exposition and trusts her leads -- in this case, a terrific Ben Foster in a rare contemplative role, and knock-out New Zealand newcomer Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: [Director Debra Granik] focuses on the humanity of the characters without ever judging them.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: The simple story touches on themes of trauma and loss, belonging and technology. But it does so effortlessly by focusing on a relationship between a father and daughter.
reviews.author: Catherine Capellaro

reviews.text: A father and daughter story of haunting beauty.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Leave No Trace finds its tension in the growing gap between father and daughter as Tom's worldview widens while Will's closes in.
reviews.author: Joey Keogh

reviews.text: Setting Leave No Trace in the wilderness allows Granik to portray an extremely enmeshed - yet, under the circumstances, healthy - father-daughter relationship.
reviews.author: Gillie Collins

reviews.text: McKenzie and Foster serve as compelling guides on Granik's emotional journey.
reviews.author: Rita Cannon

reviews.text: To hide out in a national park takes the grace, stealth and skill of a wild animal. Will and his 13-year-old daughter have been doing just that in Portland, Oregon, living peacefully off the grid, when the long arms of the law close in.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Quiet and somber, with long stretches of little to no dialogue, Leave No Trace isn't likely to appeal to everyone, especially with its purposefully vague approach to storytelling and deliberate obfuscation of details.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: In essence, Leave No Trace, reinforces why independent filmmaking continues to capture what mainstream films often cannot--human nature exposed to the elements.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: If Leave No Trace isn't quite as formidable as Debra Granik's Winter's Bone, it's still a potent drama marked by a superlative turn from teenage actress Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Understated sound design - from a helicopter drone to the hum of bees - subtly amplifies the film's themes of trauma and trust, independence and belonging.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: It's an evocative film that allows you to immerse yourself in the characters and analyze your own lives. It may not be a 'fun' film per se, but the emotional resonance is what I love about independent cinema.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Director Debra Granik does an amazing job.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is the perfect antidote for those wanting something other than multi-million dollar blockbusters and flashy awards bait.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: A tremendously affecting film that never resorts to cheap manipulation.
reviews.author: Jack Blackwell

reviews.text: It's an emancipative, heartbreaking experience with humanity galore.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: [Director Debra Granik] presents a nuanced, thought-provoking story about life on the fringes, and along the way, discovers and nurtures another star-caliber young talent in McKenzie with Leave No Trace.
reviews.author: Brandy McDonnell

reviews.text: As the father's doomed ideal collapses, the movie's conflict resolves into two competing universal impulses: the desire to be noticed and the desire to disappear.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: At bottom, Leave No Trace is about human bonds, and specifically the bond of parents and children.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: ...the film's quiet pace and beautiful cinematography (much of it shot in the forests near Portland, Oregon) perfectly complement the story.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: To call the film's lead characters isolationists seems unfair: they simply find their own human connections through privacy. Who are we to say what defines a home?
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: With harmonious felicity, Foster and McKenzie trace Granik's story like a twig parting sand. She couldn't have asked for a better duo.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: America isn't broken-it's shattered. Every frame, every moment, every performance in director Debra Granik's quietly devastating and haunting survival saga tells us so.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: Like Captain Fantastic from a couple of years ago, but with much more art, grace, and a sense of actual danger, Leave No Trace restates the male Gen-X narrative of protecting children from the outside world and their eventual reintegration into it.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Narratively, LEAVE NO TRACE falls flat, yet [Thomasin] McKenzie's performance is unlike anything that's been shown this year.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: The past decade hasn't diminished Debra Granik's formidable talent behind the camera, her deep emotional sensitivity, or her genuine fascination with a slower, forgotten kind of American life.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: The chemistry between Foster and McKenzie is brutal and together they have been the fundamental key so that Leave No Trace is one of those small films in dimensions but enormous in importance and depth. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Martín

reviews.text: Every single person in Leave No Trace is seen and depicted as just that: a person, a human being, a significant Other.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: Headlined by twin incredible performance from Ben Foster and Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie, this movie just makes you ache.
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: Very, very good acting. I do wish some more happened, though.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: Debra Granik continues to peer into the grungy sideshow of backcountry American life.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: director Debra Granik...has created a film rooted in realistic details of wilderness life that's a sympathetic but unsentimental comment on conventional and alternative societies.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Ben Foster has rarely been better than he is here.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Foster and McKenzie are fantastic. The authentic performances drive this beautiful story filled with hope and heartbreak. The audience is rooting for these two in a world that can be very harsh.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a heartfelt road picture in which the road is both the lure and the prison.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: A deeply affecting tale of love and survival
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a powerful and devastating call for help for ill veterans, a love letter to nature and familial love. Mackenzie is effortlessly lifelike in a stunning, delicate performance and Foster is as usual, stellar and dominant.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Granik's star-making instincts are as sharp as ever.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: This is a real, beautiful, quiet movie.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: Like "Winter's Bone," "Leave No Trace" doesn't unfold with a typical Hollywood-type narrative. Instead of the dramatic highs and lows, it proceeds in a stately, evenly paced manner that smacks of authentic life.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: My favorite movie of the summer is the quiet masterpiece Leave No Trace, directed by Debra Granik.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: Serves as a reminder of all the amazing things American independent cinema could be if it pushed itself more.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: I loved this film.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: These are two empathetic people reconciling the fact their boundless love is no match for the widening chasm of personal urgency between them.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Leave No Trace, in the biggest of ironies, leaves the greatest of traces upon us.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Beautifully written and powerfully performed by the two leads, Debra Granik's Leave No Trace is a subtle moving story with complexity and heart.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The subtle ways we witness [Tom's] epiphany, her little flickers of rebellion, are striking.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: One of the most gentle and unique films to be released so far in 2018.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: I was completely immersed in Leave No Trace. The pacing is perfect and while I tend to believe that 2 hours is too long for most films, this one never dragged.
reviews.author: Lindsay Pugh

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is an absolute gem.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: With genuine performances and artistically skilled direction and cinematography, we are brought into their world, experiencing their every thought and emotion and ultimately leaving us breathless and awestruck.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: It is a testament to Granik's storytelling prowess that she sees no need to ratchet up the tension when the going gets tough for Will and Tom, and the film is stronger because of it.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: The film captures the universal dynamic between teens and their parents, but the stakes are unfamiliar. Yet, Foster and McKenzie present a level of humanity that is timelessly authentic.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: As a coming of age tale it is sparse, bittersweet and desperately powerful - change is pulling these two interwoven lives apart, made explicit by Granik's empathy and unerring eye.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: Granik only sees hope and endurance in her worn out characters. They are people struggling to decide which future makes the most sense living in a country suffering its own identity crisis. Her optimism feels as essential as the wind in the trees.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a small film, but a quietly memorable one.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: An awesome off the grid survivalist drama.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: There are few, if any, villains in Leave No Trace. There are no definitive bad or good guys -- just real people with real-world problems trying really hard to stay out of trouble and stay alive.
reviews.author: Laura McPhee

reviews.text: The middle of a forest in Portland is the unlikely setting for this touching story from writer director Debra Granik as it explores the bond between father and daughter.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: We become the mute voice of society, quietly judging, urging for conformity so that all feels right in the world. Yet, that's the very thing this movie refuses to reconcile. Nothing is "right in the world."
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Both Foster and McKenzie display a profound respect for their characters and the journey towards peace that doesn't always keep them at the same pace.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: Compelling and compassionate, it's a powerful character study.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Adapted by director/co-writer Debra Granik and Anne Rosselini from Peter Rock's 2009 novel "My Abandonment," Granik shows the same profound, compassionate understanding of human relationships showcased in her breakout hit "Winter's Bone."
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Occasionally uplifting and sometimes heartbreaking, it is nothing less than sublime.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: There's a patience and care to the way [Granik] makes movies, an appreciation for detail and nuance, that makes them bracingly different from any other movies being made.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Its tender portrait of the relationship between father and daughter defamiliarises our fixed, often one-way understandings of care.
reviews.author: Hannah Paveck

reviews.text: It's a sad movie that's somehow full of hope. You leave with your heart aching but not quite broken.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Leaves a haunting impression, and drives home the central question; how do we make choices for ourselves without hurting the ones we love? In Granik's world, it's not the answer that hurts - rather, it's the journey to find one that does.
reviews.author: George Fenwick

reviews.text: All of the movie's relationships, even those that last for a single scene, are quietly affecting.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: This is a family drama, not a Social Studies discourse, and in that respect, it succeeds with quiet grace.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is mostly a thoughtful, empathetic exploration of what really makes a home, and how hard-fought the battle can be to find it.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: A powerful, sensitive film that looks at those stuck between the obligations of society and the invisible scars that conflict leaves behind.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: A thoughtful story about a father and daughter who discover that kindness is good medicine.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: [Director Debra] Granik's latest cements her standing as a filmmaker of extraordinary craftsmanship and humanistic vision. She's poet laureate of the dispossessed, an artist capable of seeing both the forest and the trees.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: I recommend it as much for what it doesn't do as for what it does. It's a gentle, troubling drama that contributes to the sort of questions many of us have these days: Who are we now? Who are we really?
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: ...a movie that's willing to whisper.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Granik fills the screen with humanity in an assortment of characters doing their jobs and at least offering the rare opportunity to connect with others
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a rarity, a movie that runs its finger over a deep vein of pain without offering palliatives or bromides. That feels unblinkered and right.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Debra Granik directs with a touch that's as gentle on the audience as bees are to Tom. There is not a move, cut, sound, or deliberate stretch of silence that in some way doesn't advance and inform the plot.
reviews.author: Scott Marks

reviews.text: The movie's steady pacing and first-rate acting keep us interested through a running time of close to two hours...
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: "Leave No Trace" is almost perfect.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Granik is generous but unsentimental; allowing every character, no matter how minor or briefly glimpsed, a measure of dignity. No one -- not even a leotarded Christian dance troupe called For Your Glory -- is made to seem ridiculous.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: Leave No Trace beautifully takes viewers on different but parallel journeys, those of the father and the daughter as one can't veer off his path and the other one must.
reviews.author: Indra Arriaga

reviews.text: Granik has created a breakout role for McKenzie... Hers is a name you will hear a lot of from now on.
reviews.author: Tara Thorne

reviews.text: An arguably more restrained and refined narrative than her excellent "Winter's Bone," director Debra Granik's "Leave No Trace" is intimate story-telling at its best.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Leave No Trace's exploration of powerful themes like the power of community and the kindness of strangers turns what appears to be a sad story on the surface into something very worthwhile.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: It covers difficult ground, but to say it leaves no trace would be a lie. It definitely makes its mark.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Granik's films also convey a strong sense of place, which is aided in large measure by cinematographer Michael McDonough.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: Tolstoy's observation that all happy families are alike gets overturned in Leave No Trace.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: A kind-hearted drama whose consistent quiet and composure leaves you all the more floored by its low-volume, high-stakes conclusion, "Leave No Trace" continues 2018's welcome trend of confident, compassionate stories about those on society's margins.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: The movie, directed and co-written by Debra Granik, speaks volumes about family ties - in assured but hushed tones.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Leave No Trace will leave an indelible mark on audience's memories.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: With top-tier performances by Ben Foster and newcomer Thomasin McKenzie, director Debra Granik has captured an authentic dynamic between two characters who find themselves at an impasse.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: You can't say enough about 18-year-old Thomasin McKenzie, whose nuanced performance here burnishes Granik's reputation as a discoverer and molder of exciting young talent.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Leave No Trace might be described in social terms as a film about homelessness, but it never loses sight of the fact that what makes a home is the privacy people need to connect with each other.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Leave No Trace immerses us in rugged and rain-saturated terrain, where it is easy to get lost and even easier to get into trouble.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: In a year full of films that explore the precious nature of father-daughter dynamics, Granik's feature is a standout.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Leave No Trace speaks, not just to the trauma and the damage of soldiers who have seen too much in war, but wider questions of endurance and the soul that can touch all of us.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is one of the best films of 2018 and promises to make a star of McKenzie.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Shot on location in the Pacific Northwest ... Leave No Trace contrasts, in gorgeously evocative visuals, the green lushness of nature with the withered barrens of Will's soul.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: With Leave No Trace, filmmaker Debra Granik revisits themes of female power years after the flawless Winter's Bone.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: This movie filled my heart, and it broke my heart.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: [Thomasin McKenzie] is a massive find. There is such wisdom in her presence...You can feel her seeing everything and taking it all in. There's such a naturalism to the way she responds in every single situation.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is further evidence Granik is one of the most talented directors around - and Ben Foster ranks among the finest and most intense actors working today.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: I admire "Leave No Trace" for its minimalist approach, lead performances and overall tone, but didn't love it like many other reviewers. (Full Content Review for Parents - Thematic Elements, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: It speaks in hushed voices, makes few fast moves and requires the viewer to infer a lot about its characters - and also to fear for their safety.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: 'Leave No Trace' gets across its simple, beautiful ideas as lightly as poetry.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: With its Pacific Northwest setting, Granik evokes the same feeling and aesthetic as Kelly Reichardt...While Leave No Trace does not specifically take place in the present, it has added resonance for this particular cultural moment.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Leave No Trace forms a beautiful, heartfelt testament.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Their idyllic but fragile existence is interrupted when police officers capture them and they are catapulted into a social system that is well-meaning but clearly not a good fit, at least for the father.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: [T]he impact of this story is subtle, gradual, and filled with insight.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Thomasin McKenzie's Tom is an affecting and multi-faceted character.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: This perceptive, deeply humane film will certainly belie its title and linger in your memory.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Beneath the slight narrative, deliberate pace, and long stretches of quiet, Granik and her outstanding cast are busy flushing Leave No Trace with sadness and compassion.
reviews.author: Adrian Mack

reviews.text: Ben Foster is making a career out of playing men who either can't or won't adhere to society's rules... But as Will in Debra Granik's Leave No Trace, he reinvigorates these baleful character traits by suppressing rather than expressing them.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: Granik is one of the most distinctive filmmaking voices we have; I'd love to see her make more features but I'm also glad she takes the time to do them right.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: "Leave No Trace" isn't a popcorn flick, but serious film buffs will find much to appreciate.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: In Leave No Trace, director Debra Granik continues to refine a style of tranquil intensity. The film's images have a rapt and pared-down power, with emphases that are never quite where you expect them to be.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: Ultimately Winter's Bone and Leave No Trace could not be tonally more different, revealing Granik to be a virtuoso filmmaker of a diverse, if too brief, oeuvre.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: A quiet movie filled with heart and hope. Will Debra Granik make us wait another eight years for her next narrative film? I certainly hope not.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Foster and McKenzie are almost symbiotic here, with the young actress, a native of New Zealand, delivering a startlingly confident performance that is, by every measure, the equal of Foster's.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: I could have done with more electricity from Foster - ears pricked for danger, he seems to pose little himself - but the New Zealand-born McKenzie is superb. Her wary grey eyes seem to take in every leaf on every tree.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: It's both thought-provoking and life-affirming.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Leave No Trace's real power lies in how intelligently and empathetically [director Debra] Granik engages with the subject of America's marginalised people.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: Foster and McKenzie spark the same chemistry through their combined acting talents, an achievement made more remarkable given how little dialogue there is.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: Leave No Trace asks all sorts of interesting questions about the nature of society and the rights of the individual versus the supposed common good. It looks tremendous, and is wonderfully acted by McKenzie and Foster.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Where does Granik find these young, superb actresses? It's like she has a patent on it. But it's her skill as a filmmaker that leaves you gobsmacked; taking small tales about people living on the margin and making them resonate.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: The story, from beginning to end, is enthralling, mainly due to the anchoring performances by Ben Foster and Thomasin McKenzie.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Debra Granik's drama about a damaged war vet (Ben Foster) living off the grid with his teen daughter, brilliantly played by breakout star Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie, is hypnotic, haunting and one of the year's best
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: LEAVE NO TRACE starts off with great promise, particularly due to Harcourt McKenzie's presence, but in the end, it doesn't quite deliver for me.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Tom's self-awakening creates a wedge in their relationship, and when the inevitable happens, we are neither surprised nor shocked. But more importantly, we are not sufficiently moved.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: In her first narrative film since Winter's Bone, director Debra Granik once again makes a compelling and human drama set in the wilderness , and once again discovers a bright new star.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Debra Granik's third narrative feature, Leave No Trace, is a emotionally powerful film with a breakout performance from actress Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Fiercely involving in a way we're not used to, made with sensitivity and honesty.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Whether this insular relationship can survive in the larger world is the source of such consistent, compelling tension that you do not notice until this close-to-two-hour film is nearly over that it contains almost no exposition.
reviews.author: Carla Meyer

reviews.text: Director Debra Granik's 2010 'Winter's Bone' was a surprise stunner. So is this. Granik needs to make more than one film every 8 years.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Foster and McKenzie are admirably restrained, acting mostly without dialogue, but with grimaces and twitches, glances and nods.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It is the acting of the two leads that makes the film special.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The film's so tight and intimate and quiet you feel as if you're at the campfire sipping pine needle tea with Tom and Will.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: This sensitive, brooding drama is an Oscar magnet.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: McKenzie's performance is shocking in its confident nuance and seemingly effortless naturalism, making every moment feel bracingly authentic.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: A story of deep emotional poignancy, with a grim political relevance.
reviews.author: Pamela Hutchinson

reviews.text: Every year a handful of small, independent American films show up that leave you breathless. Leave No Trace is one of them.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Debra Granik's first feature since Winter's Bone is another backwoods winner. Foster and Harcourt McKenzie are standouts in drama about a powerful father-daughter bond.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It's clear from watching "Leave No Trace" that these are people, and this is a story, that Granik cares deeply about. It's rarer than you think to watch a movie in which this is the case.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Beautifully shot, lyrical, and heartfelt, 'Leave No Trace' is also missing some of the edge that made 'Winter's Bone' so memorable.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Thomasin McKenzie's performance blew my mind. Ben Foster says more with a look than most can with pages of dialogue. Terrific telling of hopelessness, homelessness and hope.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: By the end, though, Will and Tom feel all too human. And their predicament will have you in tears.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: An immensely moving portrait of a father and daughter who love each other, and who can't bear to be apart.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: With understated portrayals by both leads and a meticulous attention to detail, the film is both tender and evocative.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Debra Granik is an exceptional filmmaker. Her output is small but each film is resolute and genuine. Her latest, Leave No Trace, maintains the high standards she's set. Leave No Trace is one of the best films I've seen this year.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: The beautifully observed details of this heroine's journey are heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: ...never less than utterly arresting.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: While the meandering pace, which doesn't create any sense of urgency, may be a bit slow for some viewers, this is a richly drawn and rewarding film that stays with you.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: A thoughtful meditation on parents and children, on damage and courage, on communities we create, and on what we mean by home.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The director, Debra Granik, made a stunning feature eight years ago: "Winter's Bone,"... Here's another stunner, and another revelation in the calmly radiant person of Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: [Granik] brings McKenzie to the forefront. The young actress projects the dazed yet intelligent innocence of someone unfamiliar with the modern world.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Despite Leave No Trace's humorless treatment and tragedy of its issues, McKenzie's incandescent ebullience blazes.
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is a gorgeous story about adolescence, about basic human kindness, about separation and reconciliation, about the limits of what parents can teach their kids.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Granik gives her characters room enough to breathe so we get a full sense of just how precarious their lives really are.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: [Thomasin McKenzie's] acting, like Foster's, is flawless, and their father-daughter rapport rings true from the film's first moments.
reviews.author: Victoria Albert

reviews.text: Little is said and little happens - it's inaction-packed, if you like - yet it pulls you in and keeps you pulled in. I'm still turning it over in my mind days later. It will certainly leave a trace in you, in other words.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Debra Granik has a gift for cinematic spaces that are vibrantly, palpably alive, and for putting you in places, whether modest homes or the great outdoors, that make you feel as if you're standing right alongside her characters.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: This gentle, miracle of a film is almost an antidote to Matt Ross' "Captain Fantastic," which explores similar themes in a comparatively showy, crude fashion.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Leave No Trace is better than all its forebears.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: The movie shines a gentle but insistent light on America's underclass and walking wounded, the people in the cracks just getting by.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: "Leave No Trace" is a beautiful film, heartbreaking in the self-awareness - both existing and burgeoning - of its characters.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: While there's sadness in the movie, it's countered with hope, and Granik's faith in humanity proves contagious.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Unlike Sean Penn's 'Into the Wild', which also explores the quiet radicalism of disappearing off the grid, there's no big emotional swells here. 'Leave No Trace' is a more hushed, contemplative movie.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Leave No Trace lacks the ferocity that drove Granik's earlier features, as well as a ready hook for audiences; but it offers deeper sorrow and greater hope, as well as a direct line to a substratum of the American imagination.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: The movie belongs to McKenzie, whose extraordinary performance as daughter Tom is heartbreaking, inspiring, and unforgettable.
reviews.author: Ned Lannamann

reviews.text: Leave No Trace asserts, with exquisite humanity and a long bittersweet sigh, that the best the broken can do is disappear before they break anyone else.
reviews.author: Dom Sinacola

reviews.text: It sneaks up on you, then leaves you in paralyzed shock.
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: Granik charts the evolution of their relationship in microscopic detail, harvesting from the smallest gestures the sort of emotion that screenwriters spend pages trying to rustle up.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Debra Granik, director and co-writer of Winter's Bone, is back with another-slightly more low-key, but still riveting-story of "the other America."
reviews.author: Maria Garcia

reviews.text: The brilliance of Leave No Trace lies in its understatement.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The jeopardy remains muted and subterranean until it sprouts at the very end.
reviews.author: Jasper Rees

reviews.text: A slow-burning drama infused with both sadness and hope.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: This is a delicate, heartfelt character drama built around two of the best performances you are likely to see all year - and will leave you hoping that it doesn't take as long for Granik's next film to enter production.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Tension, some peril in intense father-daughter drama.
reviews.author: Michael Ordoña

reviews.text: Granik doesn't spell out the connection between these characters. She doesn't have to. You feel it.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: When civilization feels threatened, starting over in the woods seems not only appealing, but maybe even necessary. Especially when seen though Granik's discerning eye. How lucky we are to have her work.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Harrowing and enthralling in equal measures, it's a challenging and rewarding experience.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Their journey from here may not be all that surprising, but it's a testament to the actors and director that it remains riveting throughout.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Refreshingly, there's no artificial conflict... Confident filmmaking shows in every frame.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Every moment and every character is charged with raw and real emotion. Describing Leave No Trace as a tearjerker barely scratches the surface.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: An equally tender and devastating father-and-daughter effort that's handled with supreme sensitivity and shot with unwavering kindness.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: It is small and, story-wise, slight, but quietly powerful in its detail and compassion.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: This is a film strongly invested in those marginalised by society.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: "Leave No Trace" should, by rights, be dull... Yet the movie's patient progress is driven and tensed, and you feel that, at every turn in the path, something could go badly astray.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Debra Granik's haunting drama makes other living-off-the-grid films feel like pretenders.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Captures like few other films a remarkable bond between father and daughter.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Granik is a strikingly observational director, and she takes great care to avoid leading viewers in any direction.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: The heart of Leave No Trace is the rapport between the father and daughter, and McKenzie and Foster are keyed to each other's movements, perhaps even each other's thoughts.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Minimalistic, deliberate and largely silent, "Leave No Trace" clings to each word like an endangered species. It demands patience from the audience, but that patience is richly rewarded.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: Granik has exhibited a depth of feeling for these characters that is fair-minded and gentle, offering a nation's most broken and isolated progeny a safe fictional harbor in her film.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Alive to the majesty of the wilderness and the sanctuary it offers a tortured soul, Leave No Trace is a rich and refreshingly apolitical portrait of rural America.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Ben Foster and Thomasin McKenzie are sublimely cast, creating nuanced and indelible characters that will leave you in suspense about how they can come to terms with the world without breaking each other's hearts.
reviews.author: Carl Spence

reviews.text: Judging by both her talent and the Debra Granik seal of approval, we would say that Thomasin McKenzie is one to watch out for.
reviews.author: Hugh Armitage

reviews.text: There's a lot to watch and enjoy in this film that takes the time to look at faces properly and that constructs a totally believable world of misfits and underdogs.
reviews.author: Caspar Salmon

reviews.text: A small, intimate film, contained in both scale and content, but undoubtedly solid. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Ruiz

reviews.text: It's a movie that will live with me for a long time.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Subtle but assured to the end, Granik's film is all undertow, but it irresistibly grabs you.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: A profound story about love, family, loyalty, understanding, and compassion.
reviews.author: Tiffany Tchobanian

reviews.text: A refreshing look at humanity in general, "Leave No Trace" is a universal, unforgettable experience.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: This is the gentlest I've ever seen Ben Foster. Of course, Will is still tortured. He's a veteran but he doesn't rage and he doesn't even lash out at people interrupting his peace. He channels it into something positive.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: While certain aspects ofLeave No Traceremain inscrutable, what's undeniable is the hopefulness Granik finds in those who live off the grid.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: As a depiction of a certain corner of American life, Leave No Trace is vivid and true.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Granik and her Winter's Bone writing partner Anne Rosselini have once again burrowed into the lives of the truly forgotten people of the United States, only this time they're without a marketable whodunit hook.
reviews.author: Jeremy Smith

reviews.text: [Director Debra Granik] made a film of grace and power, a story of people lost and found in America that often shows us at our noble and humble best. How rare and refreshing that is these days.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: This is a movie driven by filmmaking, and [Debra] Granik's skill behind the camera drives a lot of the narrative forward. That and, of course, [Harcourt] McKenzie's performance.
reviews.author: Adam Chitwood

reviews.text: Early scenes of Leave No Trace feel like The Road. Not the movie adaptation, but Cormac McCarthy's book, which evokes familial intimacy to an almost harrowing degree.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: It's a film that never overwhelms but it lingers, leaving its mark on the viewer.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Once again, Granik introduces us to a kind of family that cinema rarely captures believably, and she does so with a style that's both lyrical and realistic at the same time, anchored by a pair of unforgettable performances.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: It might not have the genre elements that helped make Winter's Bone something of a breakout, but Leave No Trace rivets and terrifies in its own way.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The film is consistently at its best when it's attuned to a quiet sense of harmony between all things.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: For fans of the director's "Winter's Bone"... this unconventional family portrait shares many qualities with the 2010 film, including profound empathy for backwoods characters and the discovery of yet another young talent in Thomasin Harcourt McKenzie.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: An absorbing, delicately directed and acted father-daughter drama.
reviews.author: Jon Frosch

synopsis: A father and daughter live a perfect but mysterious existence in Forest Park, a beautiful nature reserve near Portland, Ore., rarely making contact with the world. But when a small mistake tips them off to authorities, they are sent on an increasingly erratic journey in search of a place to call their own.
